# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 1 (Bu-Vb Sk1)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 1. Not wearing the sarong evenly all around

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Parimaṇḍala-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 1) is the opening training rule in the *sekhiya* (rules on etiquette and deportment) section of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The rule enjoins that a monastic should wear their inner robe or sarong evenly all around (*parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. In the verse summaries (*uddāna*) of the *Parivāra*, the rule is indexed and referenced alongside Sekhiya 2 [Horner 1966].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is shared across the vinayas of virtually all early Buddhist schools [SuttaCentral]. It corresponds directly to the first rule of the Pali Bhikkhupātimokkha, the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Bi-Vb Sk1), and the *Parivāra*, as well as monastic codes preserved in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese from the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial intra-Pali overlaps with over a hundred texts, most prominently with its female monastic counterpart Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 1 (§0.2–1.5 ↔ §0.2–1.5), Khandhaka sections regulating monastic deportment and minor matters such as the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15, §1.5–1.8) and *Kammakkhandhaka* (Kd 11), neighboring Sekhiya rules (such as Bu-Vb Sk2 and Sk56), and the subcommentary *Vinayapiṭake Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignment, DharmaNexus records a close correspondence with the Tibetan translation of the *Pratimokṣabhāṣyāsampramuṣitasmaraṇamātralekha* (D4108, §1.1–1.2 ↔ §132b-17–132b-20) [DharmaNexus].
